<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915462_theRebbe_206" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915462_theRebbe_206__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening with the heading and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">19 Kislev 5739*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains that the dispersion of Israel among the nations is a divine charity, enabling Jews in free lands to strengthen those under persecution to observe Torah and mitzvos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Rabbi Oshaya said: What is the meaning of that which is written,</t>
    <t s="1">“The righteousness of His strong ones in Israel… The Holy One, blessed be He, performed an act of charity with Israel by scattering them among the nations,”</t>
    <t s="2">And it is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader, in his maamar beginning with the words “Zeh”</t>
    <t s="3">[which was said on 19 Kislev</t>
    <t s="4">of the year 5689 at the festive meal,</t>
    <t s="5">and was printed in the pamphlet “Drushei Chasunah” of 5689],</t>
    <t s="6">that through the fact that Israel are scattered in many countries,</t>
    <t s="7">behold, even when in one country they oppress and pressure the Children of Israel and do not allow them to study Torah and fulfill mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="8">to the extent that regarding several mitzvos they are literally compelled [against their will]</t>
    <t s="9">that they have no possibility at all to fulfill them even through self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="10">[For example,</t>
    <t s="11">when there is a royal decree not to bring the Four Species into the country,</t>
    <t s="12">then even through self-sacrifice it is impossible to fulfill the mitzvah],</t>
    <t s="13">behold, through the fact that the Jews who are in the other countries engage in Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="14">they give strength and might also to those who are in the place where there are decrees,</t>
    <t s="15">so that they will be able to study Torah and fulfill mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="16">And from the light to the heavy,</t>
    <t s="17">first that they will be able to fulfill the mitzvos through self-sacrifice at least</t>
    <t s="18">[as is known that there is an opinion among the halachic authorities</t>
    <t s="19">that even regarding mitzvos about which they said “transgress and do not be killed,” one is permitted to sanctify the Name and give himself over],</t>
    <t s="20">and until afterwards they will not need self-sacrifice at all,</t>
    <t s="21">and until they will have no trials and not even hindrances and delays,</t>
    <t s="22">for they will go out to freedom and will be able to engage in Torah and mitzvos out of expansiveness,</t>
    <t s="23">as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="24">“Whoever fulfills the Torah out of poverty, will ultimately fulfill it out of wealth.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains that this charity applies spiritually everywhere, as one Jew can redeem another from captivity to the evil inclination in areas where he himself is not enslaved.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, since the Torah is eternal in every time and season and in every place</t>
    <t s="2">(as explained in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="3">it is understood that this charity also applies in places where there are no decrees against Torah and mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="4">And this will be understood based on what the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader, said</t>
    <t s="5">(in the aforementioned Drushei Chasunah)</t>
    <t s="6">regarding the matter of the mitzvah of redeeming captives, which also exists in spirituality.</t>
    <t s="7">For just as a captive in the physical sense</t>
    <t s="8">(one who sits in prison)</t>
    <t s="9">cannot leave from there,</t>
    <t s="10">so too is it in spirituality,</t>
    <t s="11">that sometimes a person is captive, heaven forfend, in the hands of his evil inclination</t>
    <t s="12">[and this is like businessmen who are extremely busy and troubled by the troubles of their business,</t>
    <t s="13">who are bound</t>
    <t s="14">(captive)</t>
    <t s="15">in confusing thoughts and cannot get out of them],</t>
    <t s="16">and to the point that sometimes he is like one who is compelled,</t>
    <t s="17">and in the language of the Rambam</t>
    <t s="18">(regarding halachah)</t>
    <t s="19">“his evil inclination overpowered him.”</t>
    <t s="20">And this is the matter of the charity through His scattering them among the nations, also regarding places of ease,</t>
    <t s="21">for when a Jew is captive in the hands of his evil inclination, heaven forfend,</t>
    <t s="22">(regarding a particular matter),</t>
    <t s="23">his release from captivity is</t>
    <t s="24">[not through his own power,</t>
    <t s="25">since “a prisoner cannot free himself from his imprisonment,”</t>
    <t s="26">but rather]</t>
    <t s="27">through a Jew who is not in captivity regarding this matter.</t>
    <t s="28">That is to say,</t>
    <t s="29">that even when the one who redeems him from captivity is himself captive in the hands of his evil inclination,</t>
    <t s="30">and to the point that he is like one who is compelled</t>
    <t s="31">(his evil inclination overpowered him)</t>
    <t s="32">regarding another mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="33">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="34">since regarding many mitzvos he is not captive in the hands of his evil inclination,</t>
    <t s="35">for the opposition of the evil inclination for each person is</t>
    <t s="36">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="37">in a different matter</t>
    <t s="38">[for just as</t>
    <t s="39">in every time there is a particular service most relevant to that time,</t>
    <t s="40">and the main temptations and opposition of the evil inclination are to prevent this service,</t>
    <t s="41">therefore the trials of one generation differ from the trials of other generations</t>
    <t s="42">[like in the time of Menasheh when the inclination for idolatry was dominant,</t>
    <t s="43">unlike in the generations after him,</t>
    <t s="44">all the more so after they killed the inclination for idolatry],</t>
    <t s="45">so too is it within one time itself,</t>
    <t s="46">that each Jew has a particular matter</t>
    <t s="47">(a mitzvah or custom and the like)</t>
    <t s="48">that is most relevant to him,</t>
    <t s="49">as is known</t>
    <t s="50">in the explanation of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, saying,</t>
    <t s="51">“Your father, in what was he most careful?”</t>
    <t s="52">and the main temptations and opposition of his evil inclination are regarding this matter],</t>
    <t s="53">And through his fulfilling the mitzvos against which his evil inclination does not fight</t>
    <t s="54">(so much),</t>
    <t s="55">he redeems from captivity the one whose evil inclination overpowered him regarding these mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="56">And this is “The Holy One, blessed be He, performed an act of charity with Israel by scattering them among the nations,”</t>
    <t s="57">for redeeming captives is the most elevated charity,</t>
    <t s="58">and as explained in the aforementioned maamar</t>
    <t s="59">that regarding the mitzvah of charity, redeeming captives takes precedence over everything, and there is no mitzvah as great as redeeming captives,</t>
    <t s="60">And through His scattering them among the nations,</t>
    <t s="61">so that the evil inclination of one differs from the evil inclination of the other,</t>
    <t s="62">through this the charity of redeeming captives is fulfilled,</t>
    <t s="63">as above.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
